messages:
laura_support: FYI customer AcmePay reporting repeated 5xxs and user-visible timeouts on the hosted API during a traffic ramp this morning. Ticket #2347 attached. Observed gateway 504s and backend 502s between 09:12-09:25 UTC.

james_oncall: Can you paste the tenant id and exact endpoints? Any recent deploys? We should also check autoscaling metrics and KEDA logs.

laura_support: Tenant: acmepay-prod. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate. Recent deploy: model v2.3 rolled at 08:50 UTC (Ashley). Customer says it started ~09:10 after they ramped traffic.

maria_sre: Pasting a snippet from the gateway logs around 09:15:
```
[09:15:21] upstream_read_error: response timeout after 30s
[09:15:22] 502 returned from runtime-pool-12
[09:15:23] pod "runtime-12" liveness probe failed: timeout
```
Looks like pods are not becoming Ready during scale-up.

dev-bot: [alert] 09:14:58 high-5xx-rate detected on /v1/generate for tenant=acmepay-prod (rate: 18/min). Ticket created: INC-2347.

ashley_prod: Confirmed: model v2.3 has larger init (cold init ~22s) compared to v2.1 (~6s). No changes to readiness probe or prewarm config in that deploy - it was a straight model swap.

ryan_infra: Checked HPA/KEDA metrics: CPU for runtime pods remains low (~5%) but queueLength metric spikes. ScaledObject shows pollingInterval: 30s and cooldownPeriod: 300s. minReplicaCount is 0 for that tenant pool. KEDA only reacts after the polling window, and readiness probe is 10s timeout. If model init > readiness timeout the pod never becomes Ready so it doesn't contribute to replicas counted by HPA.

laura_support: Repro steps I used to simulate the ramp:
1) spawn 50 concurrent requests to /v1/generate using vegeta for 2 minutes.
2) watch queue metric on /metrics (redwood/queue_length{tenant="acmepay-prod"}).
3) observe gateway 504s when scale stall hits.

james_oncall: Immediate mitigations:
- increase minReplicaCount to 2 for acmepay-prod so we keep warm capacity during ramps.
- reduce KEDA pollingInterval to 5s and cooldownPeriod to 60s for that scaledobject.
- bump readinessProbe initialDelaySeconds to 60 and timeoutSeconds to 30 for runtime deployment, or add `redwood/prewarm: "true"` annotation to trigger prewarm.
Can infra apply these while we monitor? :eyes:

maria_sre: Root cause hypothesis: model v2.3 longer cold-init + too-short readiness probe + KEDA polling too coarse + minReplicas=0 => pods spinning up but failing readiness or not counted -> slow scale detection -> queue builds -> gateway 504/502s.

ashley_prod: I'll open a fast rollback/patch PR to change the deployment probe values and add the prewarm annotation. Also proposing we pin heavy-init models to minReplicas>=1 by default.

deploy-bot: PR #4092 merged to prod: patch(runtime-deploy-acmepay): readiness.initialDelay=60, readiness.timeout=30, annotation redwood/prewarm=true; patched scaledobject pollingInterval->5, cooldown->60, minReplicaCount->2. Rollout started at 09:33 UTC.

dev-bot: [resolve] alert rate dropped below threshold at 09:36 UTC. 5xx rate stabilized.

laura_support: Customer notified, CSM oncall looped in. They were on a short hold but now confirming reduced errors.

james_oncall: Follow-ups: create infra ticket to add automatic checks when model binary size or reported cold-init > threshold (e.g., 10s) to require prewarm/minReplicas. Add this incident to the postmortem board and draft messaging for affected customers.

maria_sre: I'll capture exact timeline and logs for postmortem. Action items assigned: infra (keda defaults), product (model-onboarding checklist), devex (runbook update).

laura_support: Thanks team. Escalation closed; monitoring for 24h. :white_check_mark:
